summary: 9remote exposes an internet-reachable PTY backdoor via Cloudflare Quick Tunnel
details: The package advertises itself as a remote terminal and, when its CLI is started, spins up an HTTP/WebSocket server that is published to the public internet through a Cloudflare Quick Tunnel and forwards remote WebSocket input directly into a locally spawned shell PTY (bash/zsh/sh/cmd/powershell). server.cjs connects to a Unix-socket ptyDaemon and the daemon's message handler executes `case "input": b.pty.write(s.data)`, giving any paired remote party interactive shell execution on the host running the tool. dist/cli.cjs also issues outbound POST/ping traffic to coordinate the tunnel. A postinstall step (`dist/install.cjs`) creates `~/.9remote/runtime` and pins `systray2@2.1.4` for a tray icon, which is a benign quality note. The primary risk is that operating this tool grants remote shell access over an attacker-reachable transport gated only by device pairing / one-time key.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
